response.sql:
WITH scan_site_data AS (
  SELECT 
    s.healtheval,
    SUM(sc.scancount) as total_scans,
    SUM(CASE WHEN sc.gbsize IS NOT NULL AND sc.spanmin IS NOT NULL THEN sc.gbsize END) as total_gb,
    SUM(CASE WHEN sc.gbsize IS NOT NULL AND sc.spanmin IS NOT NULL THEN sc.spanmin END) as total_min
  FROM scans sc
  INNER JOIN sites s ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry
  GROUP BY s.healtheval
),
gb_per_min_calc AS (
  SELECT 
    healtheval,
    total_scans,
    CASE WHEN total_min IS NOT NULL AND total_min > 0 THEN CAST(total_gb AS REAL) / CAST(total_min AS REAL) ELSE NULL END as gb_per_min
  FROM scan_site_data
),
avg_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(gb_per_min) as avg_gb_per_min
  FROM gb_per_min_calc
)
SELECT 
  g.healtheval,
  g.total_scans,
  g.gb_per_min,
  g.gb_per_min - a.avg_gb_per_min as excess
FROM gb_per_min_calc g
CROSS JOIN avg_calc a
WHERE a.avg_gb_per_min IS NOT NULL AND g.gb_per_min > a.avg_gb_per_min
ORDER BY g.healtheval;

assumptions.assumption: "Ignoring missing values" applies only to the GB per minute calculation. Total number of scans (summing scancount) includes all scans in each status group, regardless of whether gbsize or spanmin are present; only scans with both gbsize and spanmin are used to compute GB per minute as sum(gbsize) / sum(spanmin).

alternatives.interpretation: Both "total scans" and "GB per minute" should only consider scans with complete gbsize and spanmin data (i.e., "ignoring missing values" applies to both metrics). In that case, total_scans sums scancount only for rows with both gbsize and spanmin present.
